title: SLA escalation: repair prefetch/warmup steering heuristic causing TTFT & tokens/sec regressions
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Customer-reported SLA violations (TTFT p50/p95 spike and sustained tokens/sec drop) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters after rollout of the warmup-steering prefetch heuristic (kernel-selector v2.3). Multiple enterprise customers escalated to CSE and SRE with production impact on short-chat workloads and bursty multi-tenant traffic.
reproduction_steps: 1) Target a mixed workload worker pool with heterogeneous session lengths (short chat + long context streaming).
2) Deploy kernel-selector v2.3 with warmup-steering enabled (default rollout configuration).
3) Send a blend of short 1-3 prompt exchanges interleaved with long 2k+ token contexts at 30rps for 10 minutes.
4) Observe TTFT p50 and p95 increase by 2-6x for short-chat traces; tokens/sec throughput across the pool drops ~35% compared to baseline.
5) Correlate traces: increased prefetch_wait_ms, increased kernel_selection_delay, higher microbatch sizes for short sessions prior to heuristic rollback.
telemetry_findings: prefetch_wait_ms: median jumped from ~4ms to ~120ms on affected hosts
queue_time_ms: p95 increased from 18ms -> 200ms for short requests
tokens_per_second: aggregate drop ~30-40% across the pool during correlated window
first_token_latency (TTFT): p50 increased by ~180ms and p95 by ~800ms for short sessions
error rates: unchanged; regression is pure latency/throughput
affected_model_variants: llama-like open models and a custom quantized variant where kernel selection path picked the longer-context execution flow
root_cause_summary: The warmup-steering heuristic in kernel-selector v2.3 attempted aggressive KV prefetch and longer-context kernel paths based on an imperfect session-length predictor. Under mixed-session bursts the predictor overestimated context needs for many short-chat requests, causing microbatches to wait for prefetch completion and scheduling onto longer-sequence kernels. The combined effect increased prefetch_wait and microbatch latency, reducing tokens/sec and violating TTFT SLOs for latency-sensitive tenants.
mitigation_plan: Immediate: Flip off warmup-steering feature flag on all impacted Hosted/Dedicated/Private routes (rollback toggle applied at 03:10 UTC).
Hotfix: Introduce a bounded prefetch wait timer (prefetch_max_wait_ms default 40ms) and a fast-path fallback that cancels prefetch and proceeds with decode if timer expires. Patch: PR #1225.
Short-term: Add a conservative threshold for session-length prediction confidence; require >0.7 confidence to pick long-context kernel path.
Medium-term: Retrain session-length predictor on mixed tenant telemetry and add an adaptive fallback that monitors in-flight prefetch completion rates.
Customer comms: notify impacted customers with timeline, mitigation steps, and offer assisted rollout to Dedicated/Private clusters.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary deploy hotfix to 5% of non-critical regions for 30m with synthetic short-chat harness (target: TTFT p95 within 10% of baseline).
2) If canary stable, ramp to 25% for 2h and validate real-customer traces and radial dashboards.

3) Full rollout across Hosted within 6h of successful 25% check. Dedicated and Private: patch delivered as configuration toggle + release notes; schedule assisted upgrade windows for enterprise tenants.
4) Monitor 24h after full rollout and keep emergency rollback window of 2h if regressions reappear.
